title: Loadable drivers and the sound core
summary: The driver layer is one of the most carefully built parts of the kernel. A header matches a package header, each class has its own publication slot, the service table is copied so IRQ0 reads it with no segment load, and a length byte makes short tables safe. The attach half and the SYSTEM.CFG parser live in images (the blob, CTRL.DRV, HIBER.DRV), so very little is resident, and each register and stamp rule came from a field bug. The weak point is LIFETIME. Nothing counts who is inside a driver, and one global worker count (drv_wcnt) stands in for per-driver worker counts. That was safe while SOUND.DRV was the only driver with a worker. USBMOUSE.DRV now keeps a worker for its whole life, so unloading any other driver stalls about 5 s and then leaves that driver detached but still published (drivers-1). Three smaller defects: OSAPI_DRV_CLASSK reports a driver loaded into the HMA as not loaded on kern_big (drivers-3); snd_release_inst calls into SOUND.DRV with interrupts off, and that teardown makes kernel calls and, in high-speed mode, DSP resets (drivers-4); and the kernel never checks that a detached driver unhooked its IRQ vectors (drivers-6). The documentation debt is heavy: snd.inc's banner still describes a speaker-only kernel, and over thirty comment, SDK and SPEC lines describe retired designs (all confirmed; the fixes are below). The systemic lessons from the peers are reference counting (GEOS, AmigaOS, MMSYSTEM) and a kernel-owned IRQ registry (OS/2 DevHlp_SetIRQ, Amiga resources). Both are cheap. The flag-day size win is a common-prefix service table (about -98 bytes of resident .bss), to batch with D1.

strengths.title: Per-class copied service table, read by IRQ0 with no segment load
strengths.why: The ISR decides whether it has work with one near compare: no mov es, no far-pointer load. This is the model to copy wherever an ISR reads state owned by a loadable image.

strengths.title: The service table carries its own length (DRV_H_DSV at +15, DRV_H_FSV at +10), and cells past it read as 0
strengths.why: Like Win32's cbSize: the table can grow in either direction without a DRV_VER bump, and a missing cell is refused by the or bp,bp test every consumer already makes, so it is never far-called.

strengths.title: The dispatcher consumes no general register; the segment travels on the stack
strengths.why: It is re-entrant per task, and the stamp is restored after pop ds (51.2.4). Each of these rules came from a field bug and they are correct.

strengths.title: drv_call refuses a stray or unloaded row before it trusts DS
strengths.why: A bad BX or an unloaded row gets CF=1, AX=0, the same answer every other door gives, instead of a far call into zeros.

strengths.title: The attach half and the settings parser are not resident
strengths.why: One macro, expanded in each image that needs it. It is DOS's discard-INIT idea applied to the kernel's own driver code, and resident memory pays only for load, check and release.

strengths.title: DRV_H_KEEP is DOS's INIT break address, on a header word that must already be zero
strengths.why: An old driver or an old kernel cannot trigger it by accident, and it costs no resident byte.

strengths.title: Attach is separate from READY: no fence answers during attach
strengths.why: A refused attach cannot leave behind a worker or a volume. Among the peers, only GEOS and OS/2 draw this line as cleanly.

strengths.title: Load failures are banked in the row and reported after the first paint
strengths.why: The boot never stops on a driver, and the boot notice and the row's caption come from one string source.

strengths.title: The kernel relocates driver images; drivers declare nothing
strengths.why: Classic Mac OS needed dNeedLock and handles for this. Here the kernel owns every word that names an image, which is more robust.

strengths.title: SYSTEM.CFG is a list of keyed records with a version per key, and the reader is bounded
strengths.why: If a key's meaning changes, old records stop matching instead of being misread. A truncated or hostile file costs only the settings it did not carry.

strengths.title: The tone router's grant, steal and release each happen in one cli window, behind a boot gate
strengths.why: A tick can never retire a newer owner's tone, and nothing reads .bss before snd_init has written it.

strengths.title: OSAPI_DRV_CALL's fence is a published cell (DSV_PKGCALL)
strengths.why: A package can reach HDD.DRV's two door verbs but never its DSV_BLK sector transport.

findings.title: One global drv_wcnt makes every driver's unload wait on every driver's workers
findings.detail: drv_wcnt is a single byte. drv_unload_x sends DETACH and waits up to 91 ticks for drv_wcnt to reach 0. On timeout it jumps to .out and skips drv_release, so the row stays loaded, its image stays claimed and its class stays PUBLISHED, although the driver is already detached. USBMOUSE.DRV spawns a worker at READY that lives as long as the driver. With it loaded: (1) unticking any other attached driver stalls the click about 5 s and leaves a detached-but-published driver, so snd_tick still far-calls a detached SOUND.DRV's DSV_TICK; (2) ctrl.inc then sets WANT=0 and ERR=OK whatever happened, so the page shows a loaded row unticked; (3) clicking the row again sends a SECOND DETACH, and a driver that restores saved vectors restores stale ones; (4) drv_shutdown unloads rows in order, so every attached row before the USB mouse's (rows 0-4 on kern_big) waits the full 5 s at reboot. The global count also pins every driver image and every MC_DMA head for the compactor. NO-PINNING-PLAN K1b deferred the per-row count until a second driver spawns a worker, and one now does.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:4171-4189 wait loop; jmp short .out skips drv_release
drivers/usbmouse/usbmouse.asm:139-149 worker spawned at READY; :162-167 detach only raises the stop byte
kernel/ctrl.inc:7140-7146 .off clears WANT/ERR after the unload regardless of outcome
kernel/memory.inc:2127 any drv_wcnt pins every driver image
docs/plans/NO-PINNING-PLAN.md:177 K1b deferred on 'only SOUND.DRV spawns'
findings.recommendation: Count workers per drv_tab row: a DRV_MAX-byte table in .bss. At spawn, drv_pub_seg already has the segment and drv_row_ix_of turns it into a row; exit already calls drv_owns_seg_x. drv_unload_x and memory.inc's image pin test the row's byte. On timeout, also clear the class's publication so a detached driver is never dispatched. Keep or delete the global count for the MC_DMA pin per K1a.
findings.listed_as: NO-PINNING-PLAN.md K1b (deferred; its precondition 'a second driver spawns' is now met)
findings.prior_art: GEOS counts per geode and AmigaOS per device; neither counts workers globally.
findings.verify_note: Re-read drv_unload_x (driver.inc:4154-4192): the 91-tick wait tests the global byte and a timeout skips drv_release. um_ready (usbmouse.asm:139-149) spawns at READY and um_detach only bumps um_stop, so its worker outlives every other row's DETACH wait. ctrl.inc:7140-7146 jumps to .off after drv_unload_x unconditionally. usbm_row is row 5 on kern_big, after rows 0-4, so drv_shutdown's in-order walk pays the wait for each attached earlier row. memory.inc:2127 pins every image on any non-zero count. Not fixed; K1b's deferral reason is stale.

findings.title: A driver can be unloaded while another task is inside it, or about to enter it
findings.detail: drv_pkg_call_x is documented as worker-safe, and stream verbs 1/3/5/6/7 are any-task. drv_svc_call_x tests [drv_fseg] and then loads it with no IF=0 window between. A UI task that runs drv_release between those two instructions sends the worker to a far call through segment 0. More likely, a package worker is preempted inside a socket or stream verb while the user unticks the driver: DETACH and the free then run under the worker's CS. The nest frames already count non-UI calls into images (wm_tcnt, under OS88_COMPACT, which kern_big has), but drv_unload_x never looks at them.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:6619-6631 drv_pkg_call_x is 'legal from a worker'
kernel/wm.inc:11737-11771 wm_tcnt counts other tasks' in-calls
findings.recommendation: Before DETACH, wait (bounded) for [wm_tcnt]==0, and refuse the unload with DRVE_BUSY if it does not drain. The exact form is a per-image entry count (about 15 bytes a site per HEAP-UNPIN-PLAN). The coarse wm_tcnt form is cheap and safe.
findings.prior_art: GEOS GeodeUseDriver/GeodeFreeDriver, AmigaOS OpenDevice/CloseDevice with Expunge only at a zero count, and Windows 3.1 MMSYSTEM DRV_OPEN/DRV_CLOSE all reference-count. os8088 has no open count at all.
findings.verify_note: drv_svc_call_x (driver.inc:2537-2555) is cmp [drv_fseg],0 / ... / mov ds,[es:drv_fseg] / call far [es:drv_fptr] with no cli; drv_pkg_call_x's own comment says the cell takes no lock and is legal from a worker. wm_nest_pushd counts another task's in-call in wm_tcnt (wm.inc:11744-11755) and instance.inc:701 already uses it as a pin, but drv_unload_x does not. A race, not reproduced.

findings.title: OSAPI_DRV_CLASSK reports a driver in the HMA as not loaded on kern_big
findings.detail: With HMA_DRV (defined on kern_big whenever ROM_COLD is, which is the default) and .cold actually placed in the HMA by COLDHMA.SYS on a 286+, %1_hma moves SOUND.DRV, HDD.DRV or NET.DRV into the HMA pool and zeroes DRVR_PARA. The non-mega arm of the slot derives 'loaded' from the KB figure (cmp ax,1). An HMA driver with no heap claim sums to 63 paragraphs, which is 0 KB, so CF=1: 'nothing of that class is loaded'. HDD.DRV claims nothing while it works, and an idle sound card holds only its image. Consequences: INSTALL's in_todrive takes DRVU_UP, which reads CTRL.DRV off the floppy, for a driver that is already up; DOS's Memory page greys the Sound or Hard-drive box. kern_mega had exactly this bug and fixed it by counting rows (KERN-MEGA-PLAN 14.88); kern_big never got the fix.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:2216 cmp ax, 1 predicate on non-mega
kernel/driver.inc:2206-2214 kern_mega's row-count fix and its reason
kernel/kernel.asm:1121-1123, 1167-1175 ROM_COLD default, HMA_DRV on kern_big
findings.recommendation: Use the row count (inc cx / cmp cx,1) on every OS88_DRIVERS build, not only kern_mega. Then fix SPEC 51.12.3's predicate sentences and the slot header's 'drv_load writes DRVR_SEG and DRVR_PARA together' (both describe the arm being fixed, so they are left for the fix, not the doc pass).
findings.verify_note: osapi_drv_classk_x (driver.inc:2171-2223): add ax,63 then mem_owned_kba sums paragraphs before one shift (memory.inc:5063-5076), so DRVR_PARA 0 with no owned claim yields AX=0 and cmp ax,1 sets CF. %1_hma zeroes DRVR_PARA (:3941). Only on a machine where api_coldseg is HMA_SEG and ROMF_HPLACE succeeds.

findings.title: snd_release_inst calls DSV_RELINST at IF=0 into code that makes kernel calls
findings.detail: snd_release_inst opens pushf/cli and calls drv_svc_call(DSV_RELINST) inside that window. SOUND.DRV's snd_release_both reaches sbl_release_inst, then sbl_stop_stream (whose sbl_unpin is OSAPI_MEM_MOVABLE or a free) and sbl_pool_put (OSAPI_MEM_FREE). In high-speed mode sbl_stop_stream also runs up to two DSP resets bounded at SBL_POLLS (4,096 ISA reads) each. The driver's own comment says sbl_unpin runs 'Outside every cli window: both are kernel calls'. A teardown that held a stream therefore runs its whole teardown with interrupts off - normally well under a millisecond, but up to several ms on a high-speed DSP that is slow to reset, long enough to overrun a serial mouse byte. fsx.inc's bracket entry calls the same routine once per other live instance.
findings.recommendation: Move the OS88_DRIVERS block above the pushf/cli. drv_svc_call already refuses when nothing is published, and drv_fseg is .text initialised to 0, so no snd_live gate is needed. Only the speaker half needs the window (SPEC 34.3).
findings.verify_note: Read snd.inc:478-510: the drv_svc_call sits between cli and popf. sbl_stop_stream (sb.inc:1897-1955) restores flags with popf after its own window, which returns to the CALLER's IF=0, then calls sbl_unpin and, high-speed only, sbl_f_reset twice. sbl_pool_put calls OSAPI_MEM_FREE. The reviewer's 'tens of milliseconds' is a worst case of the poll bound; corrected to 'several ms' in the detail.

findings.title: 'PRESERVE BX' is a driver rule the kernel could enforce at almost no resident cost
findings.detail: %1_att reads the row through BX right after its ATTACH and READY calls, and drv_call saves nothing. USBMOUSE.DRV was already bitten: an attach that spent BL wrote DRVE_BUSY through a garbage row pointer. drv_cp_closed's THMPAL leg (drv_call_ent, then drv_release with BX) and drv_unload_x (drv_call_ent, then drv_release on the post-call BX after the wait) rely on the same rule; blank.inc's ss_call banks BX itself.
evidence: SPEC.md 51.2 'PRESERVE BX: drv_attach reads the row through it on return'
kernel/driver.inc:3834, 3878 BX used after the driver call
kernel/driver.inc:4168-4190 drv_unload_x uses BX after drv_call_ent
findings.recommendation: Add push bx/pop bx in %1_call (expanded in three images) and in the two .cold drv_call_ent sites (or once in drv_call_ent), and delete the rule from the driver contract. The boot blob is noted at %1_att as 'full to the byte', so its +2 must be found there.
findings.bytes_est: +2 in each of the blob/CTRL.DRV/HIBER.DRV, +~2-4 .cold resident
findings.verify_note: drv_call (driver.inc:2399-2470) and drv_stamped preserve no BX, confirmed. Corrected: the reviewer missed drv_unload_x as a third relying site, the .cold sites are resident (so not '0 resident'), and the blob is documented as full to the byte (driver.inc:3846-3848). Severity lowered to low: a weakness with one past incident, already guarded by usbmouse's discipline.

findings.title: A driver image is freed with no check that its IRQ vectors were unhooked
findings.detail: The contracts 'a refusing attach hooks nothing' and 'detach unhooks everything' are trusted, never verified. drv_release frees the image even if IRQ vector 08h-0Fh or 70h-77h still names its segment, and the next claim in that memory then runs as an ISR. No kernel registry of IRQ or port ownership exists, so each driver works out DRVE_BUSY for itself; EMS.DRV, for example, asks OSAPI_DRV_CLASSK whether the USB mouse is up before it probes 260h.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:4232-4351 drv_release frees with no IVT check
kernel/driver.inc:4410-4455 drv_hi_ivt already scans the 16 IRQ vectors (kern_mega)
findings.recommendation: Now: after DETACH or a refused ATTACH, scan the 16 hardware vectors for the image segment. If any matches, leave the image claimed (a leak, not a crash) and bank a code. Flag day: an OSAPI_DRV_IRQ set/unset cell, so the kernel owns the IVT entries, refuses a line already held, force-unhooks at release, and needs no IVT scan to move an image. It is the same contract ABI-BREAK-LIST L3 wants for kern_mega.
findings.bytes_est: +~25 .cold now; the registry cell about +60 resident at a flag day
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST L3 (the IRQ-hook-through-a-cell half, kern_mega only)
findings.prior_art: OS/2 1.x DevHlp_SetIRQ/UnSetIRQ with sharing, Windows 3.x VPICD, AmigaOS cia.resource and misc.resource.
findings.verify_note: drv_release has no IVT test; drv_hi_ivt (kern_mega arm) is the existing 16-vector scan shape the recommendation can reuse. L3 is the kern_mega half only, as stated.

findings.title: drv_vol_bank keeps one static pair, and the bracket is known to nest
findings.detail: drv_vol_bank stores one cwd/drive pair on the rule that no two brackets nest. deskmod.inc already works around a case where they do by pushing the outer pair by hand. Any path from inside drv_load_at's bracket to mod_need or to desksc's bracket would leave the machine on the system volume instead of where the user was.
findings.recommendation: Make the bank push the pair onto the caller's stack and the back pop it (the kentc idiom), and drop deskmod's workaround.
findings.verify_note: drvvol.inc:181-182 is the single static pair; desk_need saves and restores it around mod_need by hand. Whether a driver bracket can reach another bracket is open (latent, not shown live).

findings.title: kern_mega's drv_fs_hi wraps its buffer offset at 64KB with no selector step
findings.detail: add [dfh_buf], cx advances a 16-bit offset inside one pool selector. An FSV_READ whose 32-bit capacity DI:CX runs past the selector's 64KB wraps and overwrites the start of the buffer. Unverified: it depends on a caller passing a selector buffer larger than 64KB.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the capacity to 10000h - BX on entry, or pin the caller rule in SPEC 62.9.2.4.
findings.verify_note: drv_fs_hi takes DI:CX as a 32-bit remaining count (:2711-2713) and advances [dfh_buf] with a plain 16-bit add; no step or clamp. Whether any caller passes >64KB is unverified, so it stays a record item.

findings.title: Seven sound-only DSV cells are copied for every class; BLK and FS could share a cell
findings.detail: drv_svc is 7 copies of 36 bytes (252 bytes .bss). FM, STREAM, TICK, RELINST, NAME, TONE and TIERS (14 bytes) are read only for class 1. DSV_BLK (disk only) and DSV_FS (file classes only) are never both published. Reorder DSV_* so the common cells come first: CAPS (HDD.DRV uses it for BLKCAP_SEL), BLK/FS, the seven CP cells and PKGCALL, 20 bytes. Sound's extras follow. Class 1's copy is then 34 bytes and the other six 20. drv_svcix already holds per-class offsets, so only its values change, and %1_publish clamps the copy to the slot's length.
evidence: drivers/hdd/hdd.asm:1542-1573, drivers/ether/ethdrv.inc:32-58 non-sound tables full of sound zeros
findings.recommendation: At the next DRV_VER bump, renumber DSV_* with the common prefix first and batch it with D1's DRVC renumber, which touches the same drv_svcix.
findings.bytes_est: -~98 .bss resident, +~6 in each of the three images that expand %1_publish
findings.listed_as: related to ABI-BREAK-LIST D1 (which prices only the index)
findings.verify_note: DSV_SIZE 36, DRVC_MAX 10, so 7 copies = 252 bytes. Sound-only cells at 2..14 are 14 bytes; the common set is 20 bytes; 34 + 6x20 = 154, saving 98. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE (D1 and D2 touch drv_svcix but not the cell layout).

findings.title: Driver file names are resident although every class-row loader is an image
findings.detail: The .DRV names (about 100 bytes of .text) are read only by drv_load_at, and every caller that loads a class row is an image: the blob, CTRL.DRV or HIBER.DRV. Kernel size pass 14 already moved the titles out the same way.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:3486 mov si, [bx+DRVR_FILE] / drv_find reads through DS
findings.recommendation: Make DRVR_FILE an offset into an image-expanded DRV_FILES table, and have the caller stage the name into cp_sbuf (the CFGN_STAGE idiom). The overlay rows keep their own names.
findings.bytes_est: -~95 .text resident, +~100 in each of the blob/CTRL.DRV/HIBER.DRV
findings.verify_note: Not verified beyond the string block: drv_load_at is also reached from blank.inc:683 and xmem.inc:285 for overlay rows, and the name block interleaves fdlg_s_drive and shares PCIETHER's tail with ETHER, so the saving needs pricing.

findings.title: Dead %else arms and kern_small prose inside the OS88_DRIVERS gate
findings.detail: OS88_DRIVERS implies KERN_BIG, which implies DRV_PCIETH. So drv_cls_svc_x's %else (a retired compacted-index scheme), DRV_CALLMAX's %else, drv_load_at's DRVE_TWICE arm and the nested KERN_BIG/OS88_DRIVERS tests never assemble on any build. CFG_DATA's and CFG_NB's kern_small arms are expanded only inside the gate, and the DRV_MAX=4 essay describes a kern_small SYSTEM.CFG bit layout for a kernel that reads no SYSTEM.CFG.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead arms and their prose (the prose is corrected in this pass's doc fixes; the arms are a code change for the 'now' phase).
findings.verify_note: kernel.asm:979-981 defines OS88_DRIVERS only under KERN_BIG; driver.inc:44-46 defines DRV_PCIETH under KERN_BIG. A nesting walk puts 1941 inside two OS88_DRIVERS blocks, 1635 inside OS88_DRIVERS+KERN_BIG's %else, 3460 inside OS88_DRIVERS+DRV_PCIETH's %else; CFG_DATA expands only at 5394 and 6255, both inside the block opened at 3398.

findings.title: drv_boot_x writes CH and nothing reads it
findings.detail: xor ch,ch and mov ch,1 have no reader; every walk uses CL or CX. drv_boot_want's '(CH is 0 in each)' is also false after a successful settings read, as are the 'the one CH carries' and 'CH is the loop's' remarks near them.
findings.recommendation: Delete both stores and the comments.
findings.verify_note: grep of drv_boot_x's extent finds CH written at 5799 and 5820 and never read; the count and load walks use CL, the third walk xor cx,cx / inc cx.

findings.title: Every sound dispatch pays a .text-to-.cold far hop
findings.detail: The FM/stream/tone path is: X stub, osapi_snd_fm, snd_req_inst, the .text thunk far into .cold, drv_svc_call_x, wm_nest_pushd, the far call, PKG_DISP's call bp, the driver, wm_nest_pop. Estimated (not measured) at about 300 cycles (about 65 us at 4.77 MHz) per verb, about 4% of an XT for 9-voice note traffic at 30 Hz. DSV_TICK takes the same thunk 18.2 times a second inside IRQ0. drv_svc_call_x is about 40 bytes and could live in .text, which drops one far call and retf (about 50 cycles).
findings.recommendation: Measure with a counter first (PERFORMANCE.md rule 4). If the figure holds, move drv_svc_call_x to .text and delete the thunk.
findings.verify_note: The thunk exists (kernel.asm:8311) and its own comment prices the far call at ~6 us; the 300-cycle total is the reviewer's estimate and must be measured before acting.

findings.title: OSAPI_FSX_SPK skips the 34.9 stream interlock that its close announces
findings.detail: osapi_snd_play asks snd_str_busy with DL=1 before it takes channel 2. osapi_fsx_spk's open does not ask, yet its close (through spk_pcm_idle) tells the driver DL=0. A PCM_BG stream that is already playing is not refused at the bracket's open.
findings.recommendation: Either ask at the open, or state in SPEC 34.11 that the bracket coexists with a stream.
findings.verify_note: osapi_snd_play calls snd_str_busy DL=1 (snd.inc:934-935); osapi_fsx_spk's .open tests sch_fast and snd_pcm_busy only (:1100-1108); spk_pcm_idle calls snd_str_busy DL=0 (:262-265).

findings.title: A class is both a service type and a single slot, so drivers of one type are mutually exclusive
findings.detail: One publication slot per class means one driver per class. File redirection has used up four class numbers (5, 8, 9, 10), each an ABI constant plus a 36-byte drv_svc copy and fptr/owner words resident. ETHER.DRV and PCIETHER.DRV exclude each other (DRVE_CLASS). Volumes already record their class (DV_CLASS). A table of N attached-driver slots, each tagged with a type, would let file drivers coexist with no new constants: volumes would record a slot, and packages would ask for the first slot of a type.
findings.recommendation: At the flag day, together with D1 and drivers-9, replace the classes with typed slots.
findings.bytes_est: ~0 to -40 resident (drv_svcix goes; the arrays are sized by slot count)
findings.prior_art: MMSYSTEM device IDs (waveOutGetNumDevs), the Mac Device Manager unit table and the DOS device chain all allow many devices of one type.
findings.verify_note: drv_load_at (driver.inc:3449-3462) refuses a second row of an owned class; the comment itself names per-volume class resolution as the coexistence route. Design rethink, not a defect.

findings.title: The private ABIs (VX/XM/HD) are versioned by hand and are not covered by the ABI lock
findings.detail: vxabi.inc exports pointers into kernel state and says 'bump on ANY change'. Nothing fails the build if it changes without a bump. tools/abi.lock.json fingerprints only PKG_FMT and DRV_VER. XMEM's ABI is a pair of mirrors that t_mirror guards for numbers only, whereas vxabi.inc is shared source for both sides, which is the better shape. (t_install checks that HDDTOOL.DRV's header carries HD_ABI_VER, not that a change bumped it.)
findings.recommendation: Fingerprint vxabi.inc and the XMEM and HDD ABI blocks in tools/abilock.py against VX_ABI_VER, XM_ABI_VER and HD_ABI_VER, and move XMEM's ABI to a shared include.
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST P2 (recorded as 'moves freely'; this adds a check that a move bumps the version)
findings.verify_note: abi.lock.json has keys DRV_VER, PKG_FMT, _, history only; no tool fingerprints VX_ABI_VER/XM_ABI_VER/HD_ABI_VER.

findings.title: SYSTEM.CFG drops records it does not know at every save
findings.detail: Rule 1 loses newer settings whenever a disk alternates between an older and a newer kernel (an update, live media against a floppy), and also between kern_emu and kern_big for keys only one of them has. Windows INI files and Mac preference resources keep keys they do not understand.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:5216-5276 cpc_ser writes the table only
findings.recommendation: Record. A copy-through of unknown records in cpc_ser would need the old file re-read at save.
findings.verify_note: Rule 1's drop is stated in the CFG_DATA comments (driver.inc:1029-1031 'an unknown key is DROPPED rather than carried (SPEC.md 51.5 rule 1)'); deliberate, so record-only is right.

doc_fixes.old_text:
; exclusive clips), snd_tick (the one scheduler touch-point), and the three
; os8088 API slot targets - caps, tone, play.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; exclusive clips), snd_tick (the one scheduler touch-point), and the os8088
; API slot targets - caps, tone, play, FM and stream (SOUND.DRV's, reached
; through drv_svc) and the bracket's OSAPI_FSX_SPK.
doc_fixes.why: snd.inc holds osapi_snd_fm (:748), the stream body (:785) and osapi_fsx_spk (:1082) as well as caps/tone/play.

doc_fixes.old_text:
; THE PC SPEAKER IS THE ONLY SINK. The Sound Blaster and OPL2 drivers, the
; driver table that chose between them, the per-tier route overrides and the
; Control Panel page that set them are all gone, and with them the 64KB
; SND_SEG they needed for DMA buffers, a record ring and a staging pool. What
; is left needs no buffer at all: osapi_snd_play takes the caller's ES:SI and
; paces it out of the caller's own memory, which is the shape a future
; play-a-WAV package wants - the samples are the app's problem, not the
; kernel's.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; THE PC SPEAKER IS THE ONLY RESIDENT SINK. The card tiers - OPL2, Sound

;      image claimed and the row loaded - a leak, never a free under a CS
;      that still points into it.
doc_fixes.why: drv_unload_x waits up to 91 ticks on [drv_wcnt] after DETACH and skips drv_release on timeout (kernel/driver.inc:4171-4189); USBMOUSE.DRV's detach only raises um_stop (usbmouse.asm:162-167) and spawns at READY.

doc_fixes.old_text:
1. A driver cannot spawn from **attach** — `drv_publish` arms the fence only
   after attach returns. Spawn from a service call, which is where a stream
   opens anyway.
2. **`DRVV_DETACH` must not return until the worker is gone.** `drv_unload`
   frees the driver's image the moment detach returns, and a worker still on
   the run queue leaves the scheduler holding a stack frame whose CS points
   at memory the next heap claim takes. `sbl_detach` is the reference: it
   stops the stream, then spins on its own liveness byte with
   `OSAPI_TASK_YIELD` until the worker clears it.
doc_fixes.new_text:
1. A driver cannot spawn from **attach** — `drv_publish` arms the fence only
   after attach returns. Spawn from `DRVV_READY` (§51.2.2) or a service call,
   which is where a stream opens anyway.
2. **`DRVV_DETACH` tells the workers to die, and the kernel waits for the
   deaths.** `drv_unload` waits, bounded at about five seconds of ticks, for
   `[drv_wcnt]` — raised inside the spawn's IF=0 window, lowered inside
   `task_exit`'s — to reach zero before it frees the image, so no task's CS
   still points into it; a worker that never exits leaves the row loaded and
   the image claimed, a leak rather than a free under a live CS.
   `sbl_detach` stops the stream and waits on its own liveness byte as well,
   but only to order the worker's last card access before its DSP reset;
   `USBMOUSE.DRV`'s detach only raises its stop byte.
doc_fixes.why: drv_unload_x (driver.inc:4171-4189) is the wait; sbl_detach's own comment calls its wait 'best-effort ordering... not the survival guarantee' (sb.inc:3048-3056); usbmouse.asm:162-167 spawns at READY and detaches by a stop byte.

turned "I had the hard disk on" into "I had the debug monitor on". The bit

never reused.
